more:
Dinosaur facts to drop while they color

Nobody is sure what the plates on a stegosaurus were for.

Warning off predators, telling each other apart, and controlling body heat are all still guesses. A good excuse for bright colors. Natural History Museum

Triceratops grew new teeth its whole life.

The old ones wore down slicing through tough plants, and fresh ones kept pushing up behind them. Erickson et al., Science Advances

The biggest dinosaurs were plant-eaters, not the toothy hunters.

Patagotitan outweighed Tyrannosaurus rex at least six times over, on a diet of leaves. Natural History Museum

Brachiosaurus could not chew.

That long neck reached the leaves at the very top of the tree, and down they went whole. Natural History Museum

Pteranodon was a flying reptile, not a dinosaur.

A cousin of the dinosaurs, and a fact your kid will treasure correcting you on later. Natural History Museum

more:
True things about unicorns

Medieval Europe bought and sold unicorn horns.

They were narwhal tusks, traded widely, whole and cut into pieces. Cleveland Museum of Art

A narwhal's horn is really a tooth.

In males, the left tooth of the upper jaw grows forward and out through the front of the jaw — up to about ten feet of it. NOAA Fisheries

Scotland's national animal is the unicorn.

It first turned up on the Scottish royal coat of arms around the 12th century. Scotland.org

more:
Space facts, in case they ask

Saturn is not the only planet with rings.

Jupiter has them too — hard to see unless the sun is behind them. A good excuse to color rings on more than one. NASA Science

The astronauts' tracks are still on the moon.

No wind, no rain to wear them away. A NASA orbiter photographed the ones Apollo 15 left, thirty-nine years later. NASA Science

The sun is a star, just the closest one.

The next nearest is Proxima Centauri, and its light takes 4.24 years to get here. NASA Science

A day on Jupiter is under 10 hours.

The biggest planet is also the fastest spinner — around once every 9.9 hours. NASA Science

more:
Ocean facts worth saying out loud

An octopus has three hearts.

Two pump blood to the gills to pick up oxygen; the third sends it round the rest of the body. NOAA Ocean Service

Octopus blood is blue.

The protein that carries its oxygen is built on copper, not the iron that makes ours red. Natural History Museum

A blue whale is the biggest animal that has ever lived.

Bigger than any dinosaur. NOAA Fisheries

A blue whale's heart weighs about 400 pounds.

About as much as two grown-ups. Only one has ever been preserved. Royal Ontario Museum, via Earth Touch News

Sea turtles go back to the coast where they hatched.

Every stretch of coast has its own magnetic signature, and a turtle steers by it — sometimes across a whole ocean. Lohmann Lab, UNC

A summer flounder takes the color of the sea floor it lies on.

Which earns it the nickname chameleon of the sea, and is a fine excuse to color the same fish two different ways. NOAA Fisheries
